key_insight: SAS makes attention sparsification trainable end-to-end by optimizing how context units are ranked, instead of relying on a separate selector trained from dense attention distillation. This lets the model learn sparse attention patterns more directly while preserving language modeling performance.
problem_solved: It addresses the high quadratic cost of Transformer attention during post-training sparsification, where existing methods often use hard Top-K selection that blocks gradients and forces indirect training through dense attention targets.
method: Use a lightweight selector to score context units for each query.
Optimize the ranking of context units end-to-end so selection is guided by the language modeling loss.
Replace or reduce reliance on layer-wise dense-attention distillation, enabling sparse attention learning with better gradient flow.
impact: For practitioners, this can lower inference and memory costs when deploying large Transformers without heavily sacrificing accuracy. It also offers a cleaner training recipe for learning sparse attention patterns in post-training settings.

paper_title: SAS: Simple Attention Sparsification via End-to-End Optimization of Context Ranking
paper_authors: Zhiwei Li, Lei Zhu, Hao Gu, Xiang Hu, Yan Wang
